scenes.screen_title: When execution is free, your ambition is limited by
scenes.visual_summary: A dark overview slide presenting three pillar cards side by side with icons above each label; key verbs ('own', 'describe', 'pursue') are highlighted in blue.
ocr_details: When execution is free, your ambition is limited by
what you're curious enough to pursue

spoken_segments.text: To me, in a world where execution is now free, I think ambition is summed up by these three principles, right? Do you actually believe that you've created this work and
that you have ownership of this work? Can you describe what your tastes are and understand how you can tell the model to make things better, and can you describe what good looks like? And

then lastly, are you actually curious enough to use AI to pursue other fields? Right? Are you actually able to expand your horizon rather than thinking that you're going to be replaced or something like that?

spoken_segments.text: When the camera first came out, painters who were busy focusing on their ability to recreate images, yeah, they were a little stressed out. But at that time people weren't even thinking

But at some point you realize that not only is photography art but it has changed the art world, right? And now we have film and all these other mediums and there's amazing things that you can explore.

scenes.screen_title: The generator-discriminator gap
scenes.visual_summary: Line chart plotting Quality (Y-axis) vs. Time (X-axis) with three curves: 'Your taste' (solid white step-like curve), 'Model capability' (dashed grey rising S-curve starting at 'Model launch'), and 'The work' (dashed blue curve). Where 'Model capability' crosses 'Your taste' is labeled 'Model catches up'. Below the chart is a red warning line, and at 10:04 a blue takeaway line appears at the bottom.
ocr_details: Failure: the model can generate far more than we can judge
What we control: our discriminator, our eyes and our judgment
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
| Phase | Model capability vs. Your taste | Trajectory of The work | Key Concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| At Model launch | Model capability starts below Your taste | Follows rising Model capability | Human taste leads model output |
| Before Model catches up | Model capability < Your taste | Improves as model capability grows | Discriminator guides improvement |
| At Model catches up | Model capability = Your taste | Reaches the level of Your taste | Intersection point |
| Beyond Model catches up | Model capability > Your taste | Plateaus at Your taste despite higher capability | Failure: model can generate far more than we can judge; we control our discriminator (eyes & judgment) |

spoken_segments.text: If you think of like model progress, in machine learning there's a really helpful concept called the generator-discriminator gap, right? You have two models, one

grades the model and then one actually creates the outputs. And what happens is if the grader is too good then the model can't learn, and if the generator is too good, the discriminator can't help the model improve.
We are now that discriminator, right? As model capabilities go up, at some point, maybe the model's outputs hit your own taste levels. Then it's really hard
to actually improve. And then to make things that are better, you have to go out, develop that language and know what good looks like. And the failure mode here is just not being able to
discern whether or not a model can improve. And again, what this means is we have to go out and learn again. We have to think again.

scenes.alignment_note: Jason explains the intersection labeled 'Model catches up' on the chart ('hits your own taste levels') and the red 'Failure' line, followed by the blue takeaway revealed at 10:04.
